newsitem.title: USA: Accused New York cannibal wants to be released.
newsitem.headline: Accused New York cannibal wants to be released.

text.p: A former history teacher accused of murdering, cooking and eating parts of an 18-year-old youth is waging a campaign to be freed from a state psychiatric hospital, officials said on Monday.
A court hearing was scheduled for Tuesday, when Albert Fentress, 55, was expected to argue he was ready to be freed after 16 years of psychiatric treatment.

Prosecutors said Fentress, who taught history and social studies at an intermediate school in Poughkeepsie, New York, for 14 years, killed 18-year-old Paul Masters in 1979, dismembered him and then cooked and devoured his body parts.
A year later, Fentress was found unfit to stand trial by reason of insanity. Since then, he has been treated in three state psychiatric institutions.

His requests for freedom have been turned down repeatedly by state officials. Doctors said Fentress was not ready to be released, a spokesman for the state Office of Mental Health in Albany, New York reported.
At the hearing on Tuesday in Suffolk County Court, state officials planned to request that he be held for another two years.

Fentress' father, Albert Fentress Sr. of Melville, New York has said he belived his son was ready for freedom, although the younger Fentress once told authorities it was fear of his father that made him insane and caused him to kill Masters.
Fentress testified at an earlier court proceeding that his father once threatened to castrate him.
